contract.goal: bake build provenance into every service artifact, resolve it at runtime into a BuildIdentity separate from ServiceIdentity, carry the abbreviated commit id on every log event in both console formats, make the console format default profile-dependent, and give each new rule a mechanical check
contract.output: ludwig-service-parent emitting git.properties + build-info.properties; scripts/check_build_metadata.{sh,py} registered in gate.sh; BuildIdentity, BuildIdentityResolver, profile-dependent default, commit field, text pattern and startup event in observability-spring-boot-starter; RuleGroup.LOGGING in architecture-rules; BuildProvenanceIntegrationTest in crud-service-example

no new in-repo dependency for any touched module

decisions: code-index MCP server is not connected in this session (no mcp__code-index__* tool is exposed and tool search finds none), so navigation is by PROJECT_INDEX.md, scripts/manifest.sh and direct file reads; rg/grep is used where those cannot answer

proposal.md's premise that no artifact contains git.properties is inaccurate: spring-boot-starter-parent 3.3.5's pluginManagement already sets generateGitPropertiesFile=true and services/crud-service-example/target/classes/git.properties exists before this change, with ~27 keys including git.commit.user.email, git.build.host and git.remote.origin.url. Task 1.1 still applies as written - it makes the setting explicit in ludwig-service-parent (where the gate script can see it) and narrows the emitted keys to the five the spec names. build-info.properties is genuinely absent, as the proposal says

design D4 adds a component to the public record LogFieldNames, and the encoder needs the build identity through the public record JsonLogEncoderConfig. A new record component changes the canonical constructor, which is the same revapi break D1 rejects for ServiceIdentity. Resolved within the design's own goal (additive under revapi): each record keeps an explicit constructor with its previous signature that delegates to the new canonical one, so the old constructor still exists and only additions are reported

build time day-truncation (D8) is done with maven.build.timestamp.format = yyyy-MM-dd'T'00:00:00'Z' feeding ${ludwig.build.time}, not a new plugin: maven.build.timestamp is UTC and nothing else in the repository reads it

CI build number (task 1.3) is written by a `ci-build-number` profile activated on -Dludwig.ci.build-number, not an unconditional additionalProperties entry: the build-info goal rejects an empty additional-property value, and Maven does not activate the profile on an empty value, which is exactly 'absent, not fabricated'. Key is build.ci.build-number

task 1.5 proof command archives HEAD, which does not contain the uncommitted POM edit, and writes to /tmp; run instead against a tar of the working tree (git ls-files -co --exclude-standard) in the session scratchpad. Same assertion

added a maven-antrun-plugin execution (prune-empty-git-properties, generate-resources) to ludwig-service-parent, beyond the two plugins design D7 names: it is the only way found to satisfy the spec's 'git provenance resource SHALL be absent'. antrun's version is already managed by spring-boot-starter-parent, so the BOM and root POM stay untouched

check_build_metadata.py checks three things beyond the two task 2.1 names, each with a fixture: the git.properties path, that includeOnlyProperties still admits the five required keys, and that the prune-empty-git-properties execution exists (the mechanical half of task 1.5's rule). It reads only the service parent's own POM, never spring-boot-starter-parent, on purpose

task 2.3's proof command passes `:observability-spring-boot-starter` to gate.sh, which rejects the colon form ('not a module in project-index.json'); gate.sh takes the bare module name. Ran `scripts/gate.sh --list observability-spring-boot-starter | grep check_build_metadata` instead. gate.sh's argument handling is not changed by this change

BuildIdentity.buildTimestamp is String (ISO-8601 text as build-info writes it), not Instant: a malformed explicit override must not fail property binding in an initializer that runs before the context exists. dirty is a nullable Boolean - null means not known, which is not clean

the resolved build identity is published as ludwig.observability.build.{commit-id,abbreviated-commit-id,branch,timestamp,ci-build-number,dirty}; JsonLoggingInitializer and the BuildIdentity bean bind those properties rather than calling the resolver again (design D2)
ServiceIdentityResolver's dead environment.getProperty("build.version") fallback now reads build.version from META-INF/build-info.properties through the main class's class loader

text mode (task 5.3) also leaves an appender alone when the service set Spring Boot's logging.pattern.console (console appenders) or logging.pattern.file (others): an explicit pattern is the same kind of deliberate choice as a hand-configured appender. Not in the task text; flagged for review

text pattern shape: `<ts> <level> [name/version@commit env=<env> instance=<instance>] [correlation,trace,span] [thread] logger : msg`. Absent identity parts are omitted; the three id slots are positional and empty when not in scope

startup identity event (task 5.5) is a StartupIdentityLogger bean on ApplicationStartedEvent, guarded to fire once; the identity is in the message (readable as text) and the build fields are SLF4J key-values build.commit.id / build.branch / build.timestamp / build.ci.build-number / build.dirty (fields under JSON)

ADDED BEYOND THE TASK LIST: ObservabilityEnvironmentPostProcessor now publishes spring.main.banner-mode=off as a default whenever the effective console format is JSON. LogStreamFormatIntegrationTest (task 5.6), asserting the spec scenario 'every line it writes, from the first, is a structured record', failed because Spring Boot prints its banner straight to stdout around the logging system. The module README already claimed the banner was JSON; it was not. Lowest precedence like every other default, so an explicit spring.main.banner-mode wins. Flagged for review

task 5.6's test is named LogStreamFormatIntegrationTest as required, but observability-spring-boot-starter does not bind failsafe (the root POM says only job-core does), so surefire runs it at `test` via its default *Test include and -Dit.test has no effect. No POM was changed to bind failsafe: design D7 limits POM changes to ludwig-service-parent
RuleGroup.LOGGING rule ids: logging.no-second-log-encoder, logging.no-second-build-provenance-type, logging.no-runtime-repository-access

the provenance restatement rule reports a type whose declared instance fields are ALL provenance-named (>=1 commit-like, >=1 of branch/dirty/build time/build number) and nothing else - the 'and nothing else' discriminator PresentationRules uses, so a domain object that records a commit beside its own state is not reported

logging.no-runtime-repository-access is broader than the spec's wording, deliberately: ArchUnit cannot read a string constant, so it cannot tell `git` from any other program or see a `.git` path literal. The rule reports every ProcessBuilder use, every Runtime.exec call and any dependency on org.eclipse.jgit, with an in-rule exemption list (empty: nothing in the repository launches a process today). Opening a .git path via java.io/java.nio is NOT checkable and is stated so in LoggingRules' javadoc and both READMEs, per 'encode every rule twice'. Flagged for review

architecture-rules README said 'Twenty groups, 47 rules', already stale at HEAD (25 rule sets); corrected to the measured 26 groups / 68 rule ids in both locales. The README still has no section for the presentation and uploads groups - pre-existing, not addressed here

BuildProvenanceIntegrationTest asserts git.properties hard (present, 40-hex commit, exactly the five allow-listed keys) and does not skip when it is absent: a skip would re-create the original drift. Consequence: a build from a tree with no .git cannot pass crud-service-example's integration tests and must skip them; stated in the test's javadoc
